results.title: Rank of a subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a subgroup $H$ of a group $G$, the rank $r(H) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ is the least size of a finite subset of $G$ that generates $H$, with $r(H) = \infty$ when $H$ is not finitely generated.

results.title: Inert subgroup of a free group of finite rank
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators and $r(K) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ the rank of a subgroup $K$. A subgroup $H$ of $F_n$ is inert when $r(H \cap K) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$.

results.title: Compressed subgroup of a free group of finite rank
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators and $r(K) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ the rank of a subgroup $K$. A subgroup $H$ of $F_n$ is compressed when $r(H) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$ containing $H$.

results.title: Compressed subgroups of free groups of finite rank are inert (Kourovka 19.102)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every compressed subgroup $H$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators is inert.

results.title: Rank of a subgroup (Kourovka 19.103)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a subgroup $H$ of a group $G$, the rank $r(H) \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ is the least number of elements of a finite subset of $G$ that generates $H$, with $r(H) = \infty$ when $H$ is not finitely generated.

results.title: Compressed subgroup of a free group (Kourovka 19.103)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators is compressed when $r(H) \le r(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$ that contains $H$, where $r$ denotes the rank of a subgroup.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 19.103 for two compressed subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every natural number $n$ and all subgroups $H$ and $K$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators, if $H$ and $K$ are compressed, then $H \cap K$ is compressed.

results.title: The intersection of two compressed subgroups of a finite-rank free group is compressed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and all subgroups $H$ and $K$ of the free group $F_n$ on $n$ generators, if $H$ and $K$ are compressed, then $H \cap K$ is compressed. That is, Kourovka Problem 19.103 has a positive answer for the intersection of two subgroups of a free group of finite rank.

results.title: Subgroup of a free group generated by a list of words
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Poles of a group action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A pole of a group action is a point fixed by some nonidentity element.

results.title: Characterization of poles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let a group $G$ act on a set $X$. A point $p \in X$ is a pole of the action if and only if there is some $g \in G$ with $g \neq 1$ and $g \cdot p = p$.

results.title: The action sends poles to poles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let a group $G$ act on a set $X$. If $p \in X$ is a pole of the action, then $g \cdot p$ is a pole for every $g \in G$.

results.title: The poles are invariant under the action
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let a group $G$ act on a set $X$ and let $P \subseteq X$ be the set of poles of the action. For every $g \in G$, the image of $P$ under the map $x \mapsto g \cdot x$ is $P$.

results.title: The poles as a union of fixed-point sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let a group $G$ act on a set $X$. The set of poles equals $\bigcup_{g \in G,\, g \neq 1} \{x \in X : g \cdot x = x\}$, the union of the fixed-point sets of the nonidentity elements of $G$.

results.title: Composition series of finite p-groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be a finite $p$-group of order $p^n$. Then there are subgroups $G = H_0 \supseteq H_1 \supseteq \cdots \supseteq H_n = \{1\}$ such that for each $i < n$, $H_{i+1}$ is a normal subgroup of $H_i$ and there is a surjective homomorphism $H_i \to \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with kernel $H_{i+1}$. By the first isomorphism theorem, $H_i / H_{i+1} \cong \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ for each $i < n$.

results.title: Finite p-groups are solvable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every prime $p$, every finite $p$-group is solvable.

results.title: Completely additive functions on the positive integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $H : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is completely additive on the positive integers if $H(ab) = H(a) + H(b)$ for all integers $a, b \ge 1$.

results.title: A completely additive function vanishes at one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $H : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is completely additive on the positive integers, that is, $H(ab) = H(a) + H(b)$ for all $a, b \ge 1$, then $H(1) = 0$.

results.title: Height functions
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A function $H : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a height function if it is completely additive on the positive integers, that is $H(ab) = H(a) + H(b)$ for all integers $a, b \ge 1$; if $H(p) \ge 1$ for every prime $p$; and if for every $n \ge 1$ only finitely many primes $p$ have $H(p) = n$.

results.title: The first three primes

results.title: Completely additive function with prescribed prime values

results.caption: Definition

results.title: Mazur's Problem 91 has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a finite-dimensional real normed space $E$ that is linearly isometric to its dual space $E^*$ (the continuous linear functionals on $E$ with the operator norm) but whose norm is not induced by any inner product on $E$. Thus the Banach-space form of Mazur's Problem 91 is false.
